candidate_families.description: Expose or commit selected representative coordinates as the link. This includes the current [0,3] response-link code.
Use sparse linear combinations of representative residues as link rows. Search should prefer low Hamming weight rows before dense random rows.
Use rows aligned to local block structure. These are candidates for cleaner verifier/account semantics if they preserve challenge equivariance.
Refine the existing 12-row semantic quotient with a small number of extra quotient rows, aiming to absorb response-link soundness into the quotient itself.
Random low-row links used only as negative/scale controls; not deployment candidates without interpretability and replayable certificates.
Expose enough coordinates to kill the entire public quotient kernel. This should be sound but not hiding-friendly, so it is a control rather than a deployment target.

candidate_schema.family: coordinate_projection | sparse_linear_rows | block_local_rows | semantic_quotient_refinement | random_control | full_kernel_control
candidate_schema.fiber_dimension: dimension remaining after semantic quotient plus link constraints when known
candidate_schema.link_rows: number of link rows/residues exposed or committed
candidate_schema.packed_bits: estimated packed bit cost for link rows
candidate_schema.packed_bytes: estimated packed byte cost for link rows
candidate_schema.rank: rank of semantic quotient plus link constraints when known
candidate_schema.semantic_factorization: rank-based rowspace check distinguishing standalone semantic factorization from product-quotient auxiliary links
candidate_schema.semantic_factors: true if semantic quotient provably factors through link; false if not; null if not checked
candidate_schema.shortest_bad_vector_bound: coefficient bound of shortest detected vector in ker(semantic) cap ker(link), if known
candidate_schema.status: control | candidate | rejected | needs_search | needs_exact_enum | needs_probe | needs_hiding_review

control_candidates.interpretation: Bare quotient has a short syndrome-zero vector inside the response-difference bound, but the selected [0,3] response-link catches it.
Current reviewed response-link target. It preserves a 9-dimensional algebraic kernel while exact enumeration finds no nonzero vector in the accepted response-difference box.
Sound but not hiding-friendly: killing the full quotient kernel collapses the public account witness fiber.
